answer: In a market that hires agents to map pigment runoff from a lagoon into karst caves, each new seller must post a bond and complete a small, randomly assigned survey. Payment unlocks only after independent measurements agree with the survey; an audit burns the bond for fabricated data. Creating a hundred aliases means funding a hundred bonds and doing a hundred unpredictable surveys. Deep pockets can still absorb losses, and auditors may collude, so assignment and audit evidence must remain public and appealable.
